Read this:

Ujjwal put a reminder in his phone for Nitin's practical exam, and on the morning itself he was outside the lab with a flask of tea and no speech. He did not post about it. When friends pushed for an anniversary reel, he said, "We'll keep it small." Weeks earlier, when Nitin admitted he was scared of getting too serious this early, Ujjwal had not sulked. "Tell me when it feels heavy," he had said, and Nitin had told him.

Nitin, for his part, felt chosen, and it was warm and slightly frightening at the same time. Someone had decided on him, out loud, and would keep turning up. He wanted to be worth it and was not sure he could promise everything. "I might get it wrong sometimes," he told Ujjwal on the terrace. "I'm still figuring out who I am." Ujjwal shrugged and smiled. "Then figure it out. I'll be here."

On Saturday, Nitin still went to his football game with Yusuf and the others, and Ujjwal enrolled in a Saturday photography class he had wanted for years. That night Nitin thanked him. "I noticed the tea. I don't want to take it for granted."

What did Ujjwal bring to Nitin's practical exam?
He brought a flask of tea.
How did Ujjwal's steady actions and Nitin's response show the two sides of the same relationship?

Ujjwal showed love by turning up, listening and making room for Nitin, without a show for others. Nitin felt chosen, both warm and frightening, so he was honest about his limits, kept his football with Yusuf and thanked Ujjwal.
What was Nitin feeling when he thought about someone deciding on him out loud?
He felt warm and a little scared, wanting to be worthy without promising too much.
What could Nitin do if he starts to take Ujjwal's steady support for granted?
He could keep noticing the small things, like the tea, and thank Ujjwal while still keeping his own friendships and honesty.

Harish had been in Pune for four months, and the group chat with Bidisha and Akash had gone from daily to weekly. Lectures ran late, and the hostel was loud. When a photo of Bidisha's birthday cake popped up, he felt a quiet ache, the sort you get for a house you used to live in. He sent her a long voice note the next morning. He did not count how many she had sent him.

Bidisha noticed the short replies and the gaps. She scrolled back through their messages, wondering whether she had said something wrong at the goodbye. She almost wrote, "You never call anymore, do you even care?" then deleted it. Instead she sent, "Hey, I miss you. Did I do something? No pressure to say." A day later, Harish replied, "Nothing you did. New place just eats my time. I miss you too." Bidisha wrote back a thumbs up and a joke about Akash's terrible haircut.

Akash said gently, "Some friendships shrink but don't vanish." Bidisha went on with her week and her own classes, and sent a photo of the cake she had saved for Harish's next visit.

Which city was Harish living in?
Harish was living in Pune.
How did Harish's and Bidisha's views of the fading contact differ, and what did each do?

Harish felt a quiet ache about the gaps and sent a long voice note without counting messages. Bidisha noticed the short replies and wondered whether she had done something wrong, so she asked once, kindly, and accepted his reply.
What was Bidisha feeling when she almost typed, "You never call anymore"?
She felt hurt and worried, and she wanted him to prove he still cared.
What could Harish do to keep the friendship smaller but alive?
He could send a message now and then without keeping score, and visit when he can, as he did with the voice note.

Tarun and Sabina were playing ludo on the verandah floor, and Tarun's red counter was two steps behind. Sabina turned to wave at the cat. Tarun's heart thumped. He nudged the red counter up three squares and held his breath. Winning felt enormous and his tummy felt a bit tight.

When Sabina turned back, her eyes went straight to the counter. "You moved it!" Her face went hot. "Cheater!" she shouted, and shoved the board. Then she stopped, took a breath, and said, "That's not fair. Put it back and play properly."

Tarun's chin dropped, and he pushed the counter back. Urmila, the teacher who had been watching from the swing, came over slowly. She did not say cheater. She said, "A game is only fun if it is fair. What do you think, Tarun?" He looked at his feet. "I wanted to win." Urmila nodded. "Everyone does. Let's start again, and Sabina, if he does it again, it's fine to walk away."

They played again. Tarun's counter stayed where it was, and he lost, and Sabina grinned so widely that Tarun laughed too.

What colour was Tarun's counter?
Tarun's counter was red.
How did the moved counter feel to Tarun and to Sabina, and how did Urmila handle it?

Tarun felt excited and a bit guilty because he wanted to win, while Sabina felt furious about the unfair move. Urmila did not call Tarun a cheater but said the game is only fun if it is fair, and she told Sabina walking away is fine if it happens again.
What was Tarun feeling when he nudged the counter up and held his breath?
He was excited and a little guilty, because winning felt huge but his tummy was tight.
What could Sabina do if Tarun moves his counter again next week?
She could say it is not fair and ask to play properly, and walk away from the game if he keeps doing it.

Divyansh's hand shot out and closed around the red toy digger. Shankar had been holding it for a whole minute, and Divyansh had wanted a turn so much that his chest felt fizzy. Shankar's mouth opened wide and he began to cry. Divyansh went stiff, digger clutched to his tummy, and gave a small nervous laugh. "I didn't," he said, though he had not decided what he didn't do.

Ritu, the teacher, crouched beside them. She did not raise her voice. "Look at Shankar's cheeks, Divyansh. They're wet. What is his face telling us?" Divyansh stared. His laugh faded. "He's sad," he said in a small voice. "Yes. He's sad about the digger."

But then Divyansh's lower lip pushed out and his shoulders hunched. "He was slow! He had it for ages!" Ritu kept her voice easy. "You really wanted a turn. That feeling was big. And Shankar is still crying." She waited and did not ask for more. Divyansh's grip on the digger loosened, and he looked at the floor instead of at her.

What toy did Divyansh take?
He took the red toy digger.
How did Ritu's pointing at Shankar's wet cheeks lead to Divyansh's defensive reaction, and what does it show about his understanding?

Ritu asked Divyansh to look at Shankar's wet cheeks and he said Shankar was sad, so he linked his grab to the crying. Then his lower lip pushed out and he said Shankar was slow, a way to avoid feeling bad, so empathy was starting alongside defensiveness.
What was Divyansh feeling when he clutched the digger and laughed nervously?
He felt confused and uneasy after the wanting, so he froze and gave a nervous laugh at the crying he had not expected.
How could Ritu help Divyansh next?
She could keep using calm, non-shaming words and ask what might make Shankar feel better, giving him time to move past the feeling.

Anirban texted at four: "Sorry, can't do the mall tomorrow, cricket practice moved." Trisha stared at the screen. She had been looking forward to that afternoon all week. She typed "fine, whatever" and hit send, meaning only that she was mildly disappointed. Lalremsiami, next to her on the bus, said, "That sounds cold," and Trisha shrugged. "It's just words."

At his end, Anirban read the reply three times. No exclamation mark, no "next week?" His stomach dipped. She's furious at me. He remembered she had been quiet on Monday and decided it was probably about that too. The worst explanation filled the gap and sat there like a fact.

He typed fast, cross at the unfairness of it: "ok, sorry, some of us have things to do too." He sent it before he could reconsider.

Trisha's phone buzzed. She read it, and her throat tightened. Now she was truly hurt, and her reply took four minutes to write and was two words long.

Why did Anirban cancel the mall trip?
Cricket practice had been moved.
How did Trisha's short reply and Anirban's guess combine to make a real hurt?
Trisha meant only mild disappointment, but "fine, whatever" carries no tone, so Anirban decided she was furious. His cross reply then truly hurt Trisha, so the misreading got a real reason to exist.
What was Anirban feeling when he read the reply three times?
He felt anxious that she was angry with him, and then defensive.
What could Trisha or Anirban do to stop the snowball?
They could call or say in person what they meant, or ask whether the other is annoyed or just disappointed before answering.

Lavanya shut her door harder than she meant to, and then sat against it with her jaw tight. In the living room Pankaj turned the news up and did not hear a word of it. Both felt misunderstood, and both, privately, a little ashamed. Seven-year-old Gopika carried her colouring book from room to room, whispering, "Is Papa angry?" Dinner was eaten in silence, each waiting for the other to give way.

Around nine Pankaj knocked. "Can I come in? I got scared and it came out wrong. Could we go through what you'd like and what is worrying me?" Lavanya, arms crossed, said, "Okay." He sat on the floor instead of the bed and listened for ten minutes without interrupting. Lavanya told him about Meher's birthday and that Meher's brother would drive them home. He asked two questions and said nothing more.

Two days later they set the terms: home by half past ten, a text at nine, and her location shared. "We'll look at it again in three weeks," Pankaj said. Lavanya kept to the deal, and at the review he moved the time to eleven for the next outing. Gopika, watching them argue happily over the shopping list, went back to her colouring.

What three terms did Lavanya and Pankaj agree on?
They agreed on home by half past ten, a text at nine, and her location shared.
How did Pankaj's knock change the cold war, and what did the later agreement add?

The slammed door and silent house had both waiting for the other to give way. Pankaj softened first by saying he was scared and had said it badly, then listened before deciding, and the agreed terms with a review in three weeks let Lavanya earn more freedom by being reliable.
What was Lavanya feeling after she shut her door?
She felt misunderstood and a little ashamed, with her jaw tight.
What could Pankaj do at the review?
He could check whether she kept to the terms, praise her reliability, and extend the time a little if she has.

Meenal listened as Dilnaz suggested she send her portfolio only to the big agencies, as everyone had done ten years earlier. Meenal had been reading how smaller studios now hired directly from online showcases. She felt loyal, and doubtful, and her mouth was dry. "I've thought about it," she said, "and I'd like to try the showcase route first. Can I tell you how it goes?" Dilnaz raised her eyebrows, then said, "Tell me what you found."

Six months later Meenal's showcase won her a lead role on a national campaign, a step higher than Dilnaz had reached. Dilnaz read the news at her desk and felt a small sting. It passed. She wrote: "Brilliant. I learned something from you here." She realised she did not mind that Meenal came to her less often.

They began meeting as equals, splitting the bill. When Eshaan, a nervous new hire, asked Meenal for advice, she bought him a coffee and told him about the time she'd disagreed with a mentor, and the showcase.

"Who taught you to do that?" Eshaan asked.

"Someone who let me say no," said Meenal, and slid the sugar across the table.

What did Meenal want to try instead of sending her portfolio to the big agencies?
She wanted to try the showcase route first.
How did Dilnaz's reaction to Meenal's disagreement compare with her reaction to Meenal's later success, and what did each show about her as a mentor?

She listened and asked what Meenal had found when Meenal disagreed, and when Meenal's success passed her own she felt a small sting but chose gladness and wrote a generous message, showing she counted Meenal's success as part of her own work.
What was Meenal feeling when she disagreed with Dilnaz's suggestion?
She felt both loyal and doubtful, and nervous, as her dry mouth suggests.
What is Meenal doing with Eshaan that shows how the help continues?
She is passing on what she received by buying him coffee and sharing her own experience of disagreeing with a mentor.

At Diwali, Chaitanya Uncle held up Siddharth's report card for the whole room. "Full marks in maths! This boy will go far." Nirmala, ten, stood by the sweets tray and felt her chest pinch. Nobody had asked about her drawing prize. She decided she must be the less loved one, and the comparison stuck to her like a burr.

After that she counted everything. Siddharth got the bigger laddoo. He stayed up until nine. He got the tablet for an hour on Sunday. "Same for me," she told Amma, every time, holding up fingers. "Exactly the same." When Amma gave her a hug and no argument, it did not seem to count.

On Tuesday Siddharth failed a spelling test. Nirmala chanted, "Full marks in maths, zero in spelling!" in the hallway, then ran to the kitchen, hoping for Amma's approval. "Amma, he hid his paper under the sofa!" she announced, standing very straight.

Amma, tired and stirring dal after a long shift, sighed without turning round. "Nirmala, please." Siddharth stood in the doorway, jaw set, and later that night he slammed his door. He had not hidden anything. Nirmala stayed on the stairs, unsure why the smile she had expected never came.

What did Chaitanya Uncle hold up at Diwali?
He held up Siddharth's report card in front of everyone.
How did the praise at Diwali connect to Nirmala's counting and her tattling on Tuesday?

The comparison made her feel less loved, so she counted shares and demanded the same for herself, then chanted at Siddharth's failure and ran to tell on him for Amma's approval, leaving him angry and Amma tired.
What was Nirmala feeling at the sweets tray when Uncle praised Siddharth?
She felt hurt and overlooked, believing she was the less loved one because nobody asked about her drawing prize.
What could Amma do to reach the need beneath Nirmala's counting?
She could spend a little time on Nirmala's drawing prize and praise her own effort, so she does not need equal shares to know she matters.

Amandeep wrote everything on one sheet: hospital visits, the coming exam, two assignments, cooking, laundry. Then she ranked each item by how soon and how much it mattered. Treatment appointments and the exam sat on top, and the rest could wait or be said no to. Charu did something else. She pinned a weekly rota to the kitchen wall with slots for hospital nights, pharmacy trips and meals, and asked her brother, her aunt and the woman next door to each claim a couple of them. Nobody carried the whole load. Manjula believed asking for help meant letting her father down. So she did every task, slept about four hours, and failed a class test. She snapped at her father over a small thing, and the evening ended in silence. A week later, snapping again and sleeping badly again, she stopped and counted the days. Then she called her aunt, who took two nights, and booked a session with the college counsellor. "I can't be good for him if I'm empty," she wrote in her diary.

Which slots did Charu ask her brother, her aunt and the woman next door to take?
They each claimed a few slots on the weekly rota for hospital nights, pharmacy trips and meals.
How does Manjula's way of coping compare with Charu's, and what happened as a result?
Charu shared the care among several people, so nobody was overloaded. Manjula did everything alone and slept little, which led to a failed test and short temper that made the care worse.
What was Manjula feeling when she wrote that she cannot be good for him if she is empty?
She felt exhausted and worried, and she had realised that pushing on alone was hurting both her father and herself.
How could a friend support a student in Manjula's position?
A friend could offer to cover one small task, listen without judging, and remind her that asking for help is not disloyal. Encouraging the counselling session would also help. 🤍

At two, Harish flung a spoon to the floor and howled, face crimson, until Rekha, Harish's mother, shook a rattling tin of buttons. Inside a minute the howl turned into a giggle and the spoon was forgotten. The feeling came on like a storm and left as quickly. Rekha knew that crying which would not settle even with cuddles and a new distraction was worth mentioning to the doctor, but this was not that.

At five, Harish tripped on the playground mat, barely a scrape, and dropped flat with a long, theatrical wail, one eye checking who was watching. Dressed as a Brahmana, he strung the very stiff bow that the kings had failed to bend and shot down the mark set up above a machine in the sky. That won him Draupadi.
Which notes are missing in Raga Bhoopali?
Bhoopali has no Ma and no Ni, so it uses only five notes. It is a peaceful evening raga from the Kalyan family.
Why will the Longbourn estate go to Mr. Collins?
The estate is entailed on the male line, and Mr. Bennet has no son. So it will pass to his cousin, Mr. Collins.
In the Panchatantra, how does the Brahman's daydream about his jar of barley-meal end?
He imagines selling the meal, buying goats, cows and horses, and starting a family. Lost in his dream, he kicks out, smashes the jar, and is covered in white meal.
What does the Caterpillar ask Alice when they meet?
He asks, "Who are you?" She finds it hard to answer because she has changed size so many times that day.
In The Mice That Ate Iron, how does Naduk get his balance-beam back?
He hides the cheating merchant's son and claims a hawk carried the boy off. When the merchant says that is impossible, Naduk answers that so is mice eating iron.
How did Sugriva become king of the Vanars?
Rama killed Bali, Sugriva's brother, with an arrow during their fight. Sugriva then became king and sent his Vanars to search for Sita.
How could Sanjaya describe the war to the blind king Dhritarashtra?
The sage Vyasa gave Sanjaya divine sight. He could see everything happening on the battlefield and report it to the king.
How was Drona made to give up fighting?
Bhima killed an elephant named Aswatthaman and shouted that Aswatthaman was dead. Drona believed his son had died, especially when Yudhishthira confirmed it, and lost the will to fight.
The Duchess's baby changes after Alice carries it outside. Into what?
It turns into a pig. Alice sets it down, and it trots quietly away into the wood.
How is Count Dracula finally destroyed?
Jonathan cuts his throat with his great Kukri knife, and Quincey Morris plunges a bowie knife into his heart. The Count crumbles into dust.
When does Catherine Earnshaw die?
She dies two hours after giving birth to her daughter, Cathy, on the night of her last stormy meeting with Heathcliff.
How does the jackal Curd-Face find out that a lion is hiding in his cave?
He calls out to the cave as if it always answers him. The lion, fooled, roars a greeting back, and the jackal runs off, since a cave that talks must hide an enemy.
How does Alice's adventure in Wonderland end?
The whole pack of cards flies at her, and she wakes up on the bank with her head in her sister's lap. Her sister is brushing away leaves that have fluttered onto her face.
How did Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti die?
They had gone to live in the forest as ascetics. A forest fire broke out, and they died in it.
How does the rabbit Victory keep the elephants away from the Lake of the Moon?

He pretends to be a messenger of the Moon and says the Moon is angry with the elephants. When the elephant-king touches the water, Victory says he has angered the Moon even more, so the frightened king begs forgiveness and stays away.
Where do Holmes and Watson live together?
They share rooms at 221B Baker Street in London. After Watson marries, he moves out but still visits Holmes there.
Who fought Arjuna when he followed the sacrificial horse to Manipura?
His own son, Vabhruvahana. Arjuna fell in the fight, and Ulupi restored him to life with a special gem.
What happens when Rama tries the great bow at King Janak's court?
Rama lifts the huge bow that no one else could handle and draws the string so hard that it breaks in two. Janak is amazed and gives his daughter Sita to Rama in marriage.
What is the name of Captain Ahab's ship in Moby-Dick?
The ship is called the Pequod. Ahab sails it on his hunt for the White Whale, Moby Dick.

An aquarium holds an equal number of clownfish and blowfish. 26 of the blowfish stay in their own tank, and the remaining blowfish swim into a display tank.  An equal number of clownfish join the blowfish in the display tank, but then a third of these clownfish swim back into their own tank.  If the aquarium holds a combined total of 100 fish, how many clownfish are now in the display tank?

There is an equal number of clownfish and blowfish, which means there are 100 fish / 2 = 50 blowfish.
Since some stay in their tanks, there are 50 blowfish - 26 blowfish = 24 blowfish in the display tank.
There were the same amount of clownfish until 24 clownfish / 3 = 8 clownfish swam back to their own tank.
This leaves 24 clownfish - 8 clownfish = 16 clownfish in the display tank.
The answer is 16.
There are 14 kindergartners and 24 first graders and some second graders in Ms. Watson's class. Overall Ms. Watson has 42 students. How many second graders are in Ms. Watson's class?

There are 14+24 = 38 kindergartners and first graders in Ms. Watson's class.
There are 42-38 = 4 second graders in Ms. Watson's class.
The answer is 4.

Jeremy's uncle gave him $50 to spend on basketball equipment. He bought 5 jerseys that cost $2 each, a basketball that cost $18, and a pair of shorts that cost $8. How much money does Jeremy have left?

The cost of the jerseys is 5 jerseys x $2/jersey = $10.
The total cost of the jerseys, the basketball, and the shorts is $10 + $18 + $8 = $36.
Jeremy has $50 - $36 = $14 left.
The answer is 14.
Merry is taking care of 10 lambs. Her brother takes care of 3 more lambs than Merry. How many lambs do Merry and her brother have?

Merry's brother takes care of 10 + 3 = 13 lambs.
So, together Merry and her brother have 10 + 13 = 23 lambs.
The answer is 23.

Shannon bought 5 pints of frozen yogurt, two packs of chewing gum, and five trays of jumbo shrimp from The Food Place for a total of  $55 If the price of a tray of jumbo shrimp is $5 and a pack of chewing gum costs half as much as a pint of frozen yogurt, what is the price of a pint of frozen yogurt?

5 trays of jumbo shrimp cost 5 x 5 = $25
5 pints of frozen yogurt and 2 packs of gum in total cost 55 - 25 = $30.
2 packs of gum cost as much 2 / 2 = 1 pint of frozen yogurt
Therefore 5 + 1 = 6 pints of frozen yogurt costs $30.
A pint of frozen yogurt costs 30 / 6 = $5
The answer is 5.
Annie has 6 barrettes, twice as many scrunchies as barrettes, and three fewer bobby pins than barrettes. What percentage of her hair decorations are bobby pins, rounded to the nearest percent?

First find the total number of scrunchies: 6 barrettes * 2 = 12 scrunchies
Then subtract three fewer bobby pins than barrettes 6-3 =3 bobby pins
Then add the number of each type of hair decorations to find the total number: 6 decorations + 12 decorations + 3 decorations = 21 decorations
Then divide the number of bobby pins by the total number of decorations and multiply by 100% to express the answer as a percentage: 3 bobby pins / 21 decorations * 100% = 14.28 which rounds down to 14%
The answer is 14.

Two puppies, two kittens, and three parakeets were for sale at the pet shop.  The puppies were three times more expensive than the parakeets, and the parakeets were half as expensive as the kittens.  If the cost of one parakeet was $10, what would it cost to purchase all of the pets for sale at the pet shop, in dollars?

Puppies cost three times more than parakeets, or 3*$10=$30 per puppy.
Parakeets were half as expensive as the kittens, or 2*$10=$20 per kitten.
Two puppies cost 2*$30=$60
Two kittens cost 2*$20=$40.
And three parakeets cost 3*$10=$30.
Thus, the cost to purchase all of the pets for sale at the pet shop is $60+$40+$30=$130.
The answer is 130.
A conference center has six rooms. Each room can hold up to 80 people. Today, the conference center is only 2/3 full. How many people are in the conference center?

The conference center can hold up to 80 x 6 = 480 people.
Today, there are 480 x 2/3 = 320 people in the conference center.
The answer is 320.
James spends 30 minutes twice a day on meditation.  How many hours a week does he spend meditating?

Each session is 30/60=.5 hours
So she spends .5*2=1 hour a day
So she spends 1*7=7 hours a week
The answer is 7.

Mary was working on a research paper and already had borrowed 5 books from the library.  3 books weren't helpful so she returned those and checked out 5 more books.  3 days later, she went back to the library and returned 2 of those books and checked out 7 more books.  How many books does Mary currently have checked out of the library?

Mary started with 5 books and returned 3 so she had 5-3 = 2 books
She had 2 books and checked out 5 more books so she had 2+5 = 7 books
She now has 7 books but returned 2 so she has 7-2 = 5 books
She had 5 books and checked out 7 more books so she has 5+7 = 12 books checked out
The answer is 12.
There are 9 boys and 12 girls in a class. The teacher needs to create groups with three members for their class activity. How many groups are formed?

There are 9 + 12 = 21 students in a class.
Hence, 21/3 = 7 groups are formed.
The answer is 7.
On a numeral card lying on the table, Sunil reads 9 but Tara reads 6. How can they know which it is?

Answer: Look for the line under the numeral. If the line is below, turn the card so the line is at the bottom. Then 6 has its round part at the bottom and 9 has its round part at the top.

6 and 9 are the same shape turned upside down. Put a small line under 6 and 9 on cards and dice. Rhyme: "6 is a snail on the ground, 9 is a balloon up high."
The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. How long is each side?

Answer: 9 cm. 36 / 4 = 9.

A square has 4 equal sides, and together they make 36 cm. Share 36 into 4 equal parts: 36 / 4 = 9 cm. Check: 4 x 9 = 36. Finding the side is the opposite of finding the perimeter, so we divide instead of multiply.
Now you try: a square of perimeter 100 m.
The answer is 25 m.

(a) When x^3 + ax^2 - 5x + 6 is divided by x - 2, the remainder is 8. Find a. (b) The polynomials ax^3 + 4x^2 + 3x - 4 and x^3 - 4x + a leave the same remainder when divided by x - 3. Find a.

Answer: (a) a = 1. (b) a = -1.

Use the remainder theorem to turn each fact into an EQUATION in a. (a) p(2) = 8 + 4a - 10 + 6 = 4a + 4. The remainder is 8, so 4a + 4 = 8 and a = 1. Check: p(x) = x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 6, p(2) = 8 + 4 - 10 + 6 = 8. (b) Remainder of the first: 27a + 36 + 9 - 4 = 27a + 41. Remainder of the second: 27 - 12 + a = 15 + a. They are equal: 27a + 41 = 15 + a, so 26a = -26 and a = -1. Check: first -27 + 41 = 14, second 15 - 1 = 14. Common mistake: forgetting that a appears in BOTH polynomials in (b).
Now you try: find k if x^3 + kx^2 + 2x - 3 leaves remainder 5 when divided by x + 1.
The answer is -1 + k - 2 - 3 = 5, k = 11.

A shopkeeper's price rises by 2% in each of 5 years. Approximate the growth factor (1.02)^5 with differentials and compare with the exact value.

Answer: (1.02)^5 ~ 1.1; exact 1.104081, so prices rise by about 10.4%.

f(x) = x^5, a = 1, h = 0.02, f'(x) = 5x^4: (1.02)^5 ~ 1^5 + 5 x 1^4 x 0.02 = 1 + 0.1 = 1.1 This is the rule (1 + h)^n ~ 1 + nh: the first two terms of the binomial expansion 1 + 5h + 10h^2 + ... . The neglected 10h^2 = 0.004 explains most of the difference 1.104081 - 1.1. The approximation says "five rises of 2% make about 10%" - fine for a quick estimate, but compounding adds a little extra. Common mistake: using h = 1.02 instead of 0.02.

Quick one: what is "cursory"?
Also, why does ice float on water?
What will the price of petrol be next month?
And one more: spot the error: I am having this bicycle since last year.
Then, Difference between "weather" and "whether"?

1. "Cursory" is an adjective. It means quick and not thorough.
2. Ice is lighter than the same amount of liquid water. Because water expands as it freezes, so ice takes up more space for the same weight.
3. I don't know that. Prices change with many things and I can't see them. Check the news or the pump's board.
4. Fixed: I have had this bicycle since last year. Why: "have" (own) takes no "-ing"; "since" needs the present perfect.
5. "Weather" is the rain, sun and wind outside, and "whether" means "if". For example: I wonder whether the weather will clear.

Why do we wear a coat on a cold ride on a scooter? Plus, could you explain what notable means? Also, could you explain the difference between "stationary" and "stationery"? And one more: can you correct this for me? "The Ganga is longest river in India." Also, how can I be kind to a new classmate who looks lonely?

1. A coat keeps us from losing body heat. Because the moving air blows heat away from the body, so it feels much colder than it is.
2. As an adjective, "notable" means worth noticing, or important.
3. "Stationary" means not moving, and "stationery" means pens, paper and similar things. For example: the bus was stationary outside the stationery shop.
4. Corrected: The Ganga is the longest river in India. Why: a superlative needs "the" before it.
5. Invite the new student to sit with you and join a game. Ask about their old school and listen with interest.

Is it "tyrany" or "tyranny"?
Also, who painted the picture in the lobby of our school?
One more thing: why is it better to cross a road at a zebra crossing?
Oh, and I don't understand "instructing". Can you help?

1. It is "tyranny", with a double "n".
2. I don't know, because I can't see your school. Look for a name on the frame, or ask a teacher.
3. It is the place where drivers expect people. Because drivers slow down and stop there, crossing there is safer.
4. "Instructing" is the -ing form of the verb "instruct", which means to teach someone, or to tell them what to do.

What's the meaning of the word bleached?
And "Hopeing" or "hoping"?
And one more: can you fix my sentence? Priya can sings very well.
Last one: what does "your guess is as good as mine" mean?

1. "Bleached" is the past form of the verb "bleach", which means to make something white or pale with a chemical or the sun.
2. It is "hoping". Drop the silent "e" of "hope" before adding "-ing".
3. Fixed: Priya can sing very well. Why: after "can", the verb stays in its base form.
4. It means I do not know either. For example: when will the bus come? Your guess is as good as mine.

Can you correct this for me? "Can I borrow your pen, please."
Why does music make people want to dance?
Is "acommodate" right?
Any idea what "interlude" means?
what does "last but not least" mean

1. It should be: Can I borrow your pen, please? Why: a request in question form ends with a question mark.
2. Music gives the body a beat to follow. Because the beat is a steady pattern, and the body tends to follow a rhythm without thinking.
3. No, it is "accommodate", with a double "c" and a double "m".
4. "Interlude" is a noun. It means a short break or period between two events.
5. It is used to introduce the final item in a list and say it is also important. For example: last but not least, thank you to the cook.

Okay, three things I wonder about:
Quick one: why is a rainbow seen when the Sun shines during rain?
Spot the error: She was born at 2008.
What is a good way to handle a disagreement with a sibling?
What is the meaning of festive?
what did my grandfather do when he was young

1. A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through raindrops. Because raindrops bend and split sunlight into its colours, and the sun must be behind the viewer.
2. Write it as: She was born in 2008. Why: we use "in" with years.
3. Wait until both of you are calm, and then take turns to say what bothered you. Look for a fair answer you both can accept.
4. As an adjective, "festive" means joyful, as for a celebration.
5. I don't know; I know nothing about your family. Ask your grandfather, since he would love to tell you.

Why do car tyres have grooves or patterns?
how do I find my way around a new city
Quick one: what is "contour"?

1. The patterns help the tyre grip. Because they let water escape and give the rubber more bite on the road.
2. Look at a map before you go, and note a few big landmarks. If you are lost, ask a shopkeeper or a police officer.
3. "Contour" is a noun. It means the outline of the shape of something.
Is "improper" a hard word? What does it mean? How can I stay calm when I lose a game?

1. As an adjective, "improper" means not suitable or not correct.
2. Take a few deep breaths and remind yourself that it is only a game. Congratulate the winners, and think about one thing to improve next time.

what was the last score of the school team?
Also, what does flutter mean in simple words?
And how do I spell "strenght"?
One more thing: make this correct: I wish I can swim well.

1. I don't know; I can't see your school's match records. Ask the sports teacher or the team captain.
2. As a verb, "flutter" means to move lightly and quickly, as a bird's wings do.
3. It is "strength", with "ngth" at the end.
4. Write it as: I wish I could swim well. Why: after "wish" for something not true now, we use the past form "could".

I keep seeing "possession" in my reading. Meaning?
Why do we need to stay seated during a train ride?
When does the next bus to the airport leave?
What can I do on a boring train journey?
Fix my grammar: He got down from the bus at the stop.

1. Possession means something that you own. It is a noun.
2. A seated passenger is much less likely to fall. Because the train can lurch or turn, and a standing person may lose balance.
3. I don't know that. I can't see bus timetables. Check the bus service's official website or ask at the bus stand.
4. Read a book, play a word game with a friend or watch the view and look for patterns. Bring a small notebook for drawing or notes.
5. Correct form: He got off the bus at the stop. Why: the usual phrase is "get off" a bus.
What can I do to find a lost pen in class? Also, what is "standstill"? Plus, check my English: "She always come late to class." Then, what are the latest results of the state board exams?

1. Look under the desks and in your bag first, and then ask your classmates. Tell the teacher if it does not turn up.
2. As a noun, "standstill" means a complete stop.
3. Corrected: She always comes late to class. Why: with "she", the simple present verb takes "-s".
4. I don't know that. I can't see new results. Check the board's official website.

I keep seeing "landsman" in my reading. Meaning?
Then, is there a mistake here? He lives in a village nearby to the river.
Oh, and what's the meaning of the word proclaim?

1. "Landsman" is a noun. It means a person who lives or works on land and not at sea.
2. Correct form: He lives in a village near the river. Why: "nearby" is used without "to", while "near" takes the noun directly.
3. "Proclaim" is a verb. It means to announce something publicly and officially.

(1) Quick one: what was the title of the book my friend lent me?
(2) How many pages did my friend read today?
(3) Please define "sobriety".
(4) Why are the pages of a book numbered?

1. I don't know; I can't see your friend's books. Look at the book itself or ask your friend.
2. I don't know, because I can't see what your friend read. Ask your friend.
3. As a noun, "sobriety" means the state of being serious, or not drunk.
4. Page numbers help us find things. Because they let us go to the right place using a contents list.
Why do we fly kites at Makar Sankranti? What is "greeting"? Please fix: She made a delicious sweets.

1. It is a tradition of the season. Because the breeze is good and people enjoy being outside together.
2. A greeting is a friendly word or message when people meet. Example: He sent a festival greeting.
3. Fixed: She made delicious sweets. Why: "Sweets" is plural, so no "a".

Here are my questions for today.
Vikram scored 12 runs and Yusuf scored 6 runs. How many more runs did Vikram score?
What is a good warm-up before a skipping rope session?
Fix this sentence: "He have a new football."

1. 6 runs. Because 12 - 6 = 6.
2. Roll your ankles, swing your arms and jog on the spot for a minute. Then start slowly.
3. Fixed: He has a new football. Why: "He" takes "has".

Could you answer these?
What should I do if I make a mistake at work?
What is wrong with "She is more experienced that me."?

1. Tell your manager quickly, say what happened and offer a way to fix it. Learn from it.
2. Fixed: She is more experienced than me. Why: Comparisons use "than", not "that".
Please fix: He explained me the work. Why do workers wear uniforms? How can I get along with a coworker I find difficult?

1. Fixed: He explained the work to me. Why: "Explain" needs "to" before the person.
2. So people can recognise them. Because a uniform shows their role and often keeps them safe.
3. Stay polite, listen to their view and focus on the task. Speak to them calmly if there is a real problem.
How do I say sorry to my sister after a fight? And what is the meaning of "sibling"?

1. Tell her plainly what you did wrong and that you are sorry, then give her time to answer.
2. A sibling is your brother or sister.
What does "sentence" mean in grammar? And how can I improve my handwriting?

1. A sentence is a group of words that makes a complete thought.
2. Write slowly, keep letters the same size, and practise a few lines each day.
Here are my two questions for today. What does "spill the beans" mean? What does "puzzle" mean?

1. It means to tell a secret by mistake. Do not spill the beans about the surprise party.
2. A puzzle is a game or problem that you solve by thinking. We finished the jigsaw puzzle together.
I want to pack a healthier tiffin for myself, but I hate boring food.
Healthy does not have to mean boring. Colour and crunch make a big difference. What do you usually take now?
Mostly bread and jam, or chips if I'm in a hurry.

You could swap one thing at a time. Try a vegetable sandwich with a little chutney, or a roll made from last night's roti and sabzi. Add a fruit you like, such as a banana or a few grapes, for something sweet.
The roll idea is good. My mornings are rushed though.
Then fill the roll at night and keep it in the fridge. In the morning, you only need to pack it. A ready box takes less than a minute, which is faster than buying chips.
I broke my record in the 100 metre sprint today, but my coach says I still have a lot of work to do.
Congratulations on the record. That is a real achievement. Your coach is likely pushing you because he sees more potential in you.
It felt like he wasn't happy.
Coaches often focus on what to improve, because that's their job. You could ask him directly, 'What should I work on next?' That gives you something clear.
Good idea. I'll ask him on Monday.
That shows you want to grow, and coaches value that.
The teacher said I should speak louder, but I feel shy when everyone looks at me.
It's something many students work on. Try speaking to one friendly face in the room instead of the whole class.
I can try that.
Also, practise at home reading a paragraph aloud from a distance. Slowly raise your volume, until it's comfortable for someone across the room to hear you.
I want to move my study table next to the window, but my mom thinks it will be too bright.
Natural light is great for studying, and mid-day glare can bother the eyes. Which way does the window face?
East. So it's bright in the morning.
Then the table can work well, since morning light is gentle. A thin curtain can soften it if it ever gets too strong. Keep the screen or book at an angle, so the light doesn't glare on it.
I think our pet turtle looks lonely in his tank.
It's kind of you to care. Turtles are often fine on their own, but different kinds have different needs. Do you know which kind he is?
I'm not sure, the shop didn't say.
Then a local vet who looks after small animals can tell you, and advise about his tank. A vet is the best person to ask, since each kind has special needs.
Meanwhile, can I do anything for him?
Make sure he has clean water, a place to climb out and rest, and a proper light and warm spot. Ask the shop or the vet for those details.
He likes to stay under a rock. Is that bad?
Many turtles like a hiding place, so the rock is probably a good thing. If he stops eating or looks unwell, the vet is the person to call.
Okay. I'll ask the vet at the next visit. He's called Sheldon, by the way.
Sheldon is a great name for a turtle, calm and in no hurry. I hope the vet visit goes well.
I'm planning a surprise visit to my friend who is in a different town. Is that a good idea?
Surprises can be lovely, but people also need to be ready for visitors. Does she usually like surprises?
She does, but she may be busy.
Then maybe check with someone close to her about her schedule. You can still keep the exact time a surprise.
I can ask her sister.
Good thinking. Ask her sister to keep it quiet, and pick a time when your friend is likely to be at home.
What should I bring?
Something simple she likes, such as her favourite snack or a small plant. Your company is the main gift.
I forgot my homework at home and the teacher is strict. I'm scared.
That is a tough start to the day. The best step is to tell the teacher honestly before class begins, so you are not caught out later.
What do I say exactly?
Something simple: 'I am sorry, I forgot my homework at home. May I bring it tomorrow?' Say it calmly and look at the teacher while speaking.
What if they punish me anyway?
That may happen, and it would be hard. Honesty usually earns more respect than hiding the problem, though. Accept what the teacher says politely, and bring the work the next day.
How do I stop forgetting things?
Pack your bag the night before and check it against your timetable. Keep homework in the same pocket every day. Within a week, it becomes a habit.
I'm comparing two pairs of shoes, one cheaper and one sturdier. How do I choose?
Think about how often you will wear them and for what. For daily use or walking, a sturdy pair usually lasts longer, so it can cost less over time.
The cheaper pair looks nicer.
Looks matter, but fit and comfort matter more. Try both on and walk around the shop. Uncomfortable shoes tend to stay in the cupboard, however nice they look.
What if my feet are still growing?
Then a cheaper pair may be the sensible option, since you will outgrow either pair soon. Leave a little space at the toe, and check the fit again after a few months.
My father works long hours and we barely see each other.
That can feel lonely. It is natural to miss time with a parent. Does he know how you feel?
I haven't told him.
You could tell him when he has a quiet moment, saying that you miss spending time together. Most parents want to know.
What could we do together?
Small things count, such as having one meal a week together, a short walk or a game. It does not have to be big or expensive.
What if he's too tired?
Then something small and calm might suit him, like sitting together for a few minutes. Ask him what he would enjoy.
Thanks, I'll talk to him this weekend.
A weekend is a good time, since he may be more relaxed. Say it simply and kindly, and listen to what he says.
My bedroom door squeaks every time it opens.
A squeak usually comes from dry metal hinges rubbing together. Lubricating the hinge pin normally fixes it.
What can I use for that?
A drop of machine oil or a spray lubricant works well. In a pinch, rubbing a bar of soap or a candle on the pin helps. Wipe off any extra so it does not mark the door.
We have leftover chapatis. What can I make with them?
Cut them into strips and fry them with onions, tomatoes and spices for a quick chapati noodle dish. You can also tear them up and toss with curd or jaggery for a simple snack.
Can they be used for wraps?
Yes. Fill a chapati with vegetables or paneer and roll it up as a wrap. Warm it on a pan for a minute so the filling sticks together.
How long can the chapatis wait?
Cooked chapatis last about a day at room temperature in a covered box, or longer in the fridge. Use them soon and discard any that smell or look odd.
My science teacher, Mr Das, keeps saying I have talent but I never believe him.
It is kind of him to say that. Why do you think you find it hard to believe?
I only get average marks. I am Grace.
Marks do not show everything, Grace. A teacher sees how you ask questions, solve problems and think in class. Mr Das may notice things your marks do not show.
How can I find out what he sees in me?
Ask him directly after class. Say you would like to know where you are strong and where you can improve. Most teachers love a student who asks for feedback.
Good. What is my teacher's name again?
Your science teacher is Mr Das. You could ask him tomorrow, Grace, something like, "Sir, what do you think I do well, and what should I work on?"
Today is my birthday and nobody at home remembered. I am pretty down.
I am sorry, that must feel lonely. Happy birthday to you anyway. Have you told anyone that it is your birthday?
No, I did not want to ask for a wish.
I understand, but a gentle reminder is not begging. You could say, by the way, it is my birthday today, and see how they react. Family often forgets in a busy morning and feels bad later.
Okay, I might tell my mum at dinner.
That sounds like a good moment, when everyone is together. Say it lightly and let her respond. In the meantime, do something small for yourself, like a favourite snack or a walk.
I will get a jalebi on my way home. I do love jalebi.
A jalebi on your birthday is a lovely treat. Enjoy it slowly, and maybe share one with your mum at dinner when you tell her. It is a gentle way to open the conversation.
I sat next to a lovely old couple on the flight today. They told me about their travels.
That sounds like a nice surprise, and a good way to pass a flight. Where had they travelled in all those years?
They have visited forty countries. The lady, Mrs. Dsouza, said her favourite was Japan.
Forty countries is amazing. Did Mrs. Dsouza say why she loved Japan most? People who travel a lot often have good reasons.
She said the people were polite and the food was fresh, and the trains were always on time.
That is a lovely summary. If you ever go to Japan, you will have Mrs. Dsouza's story to remember. It might be worth writing down what she said in your travel notes.
I want to visit Japan someday because of what she said. What should I do first?

Start by learning a few Japanese phrases and reading about the things Mrs. Dsouza loved, like the polite people, the fresh food and the trains that always ran on time. Having a goal and a rough date makes a dream easier to reach.
Our class is planning a farewell trip, but the teachers are asking us to pick a place within a day's drive.
Good, a day trip is easier to manage. What kind of place does your class like? Is it nature, fun rides, or something to learn from?
Most want a water park. A few want a museum. I am in charge of collecting votes.
Then make a simple list on paper or a message, ask each classmate to choose one, and count the results. A fair method keeps everyone happy, even if their choice does not win.
The water park got nineteen votes. The museum got eight.
That is a clear result. Tell the class and the teachers the winner. Thank the museum supporters, and maybe suggest the museum for another outing so their idea is not forgotten.
Good idea. The teacher, Mrs. Fernandes, wants a list of names.
Then make a clean list in alphabetical order, and ask each student to confirm. Include parent contact numbers if the school needs them, so Mrs. Fernandes has everything in one place.
Done. Who did I say asked for the list, and which place won?
Mrs. Fernandes asked for the list of names, and the water park won the vote. Hand her the list soon so she can organise permission slips and the bus.
Karan here. I'd like to draw people in motion, like runners.
That is a challenging subject, Karan. Start with stick figures. Draw a line for the spine, a circle for the head and lines for arms and legs, bent to show the pose. Have you tried?
Not yet. My figures always look stiff.
Stiffness comes from straight lines. Draw the spine with a gentle curve, and bend the elbows and knees. Think of the body leaning in the direction of the run.
How can I see real movements?
Watch runners in a park, or ask a friend to hold running poses. Take quick sketches of one pose each, spending only thirty seconds on each. Fast sketches catch the motion.
Maybe my friend Dev can pose for me. He runs every day.
That would be perfect. Ask Dev to pause in a running stance for a few seconds, and draw the curve of his spine and bent knees first.
Who did I say would pose?
You said your friend Dev, Karan. Since he runs every day, he will know good running poses. Start each sketch with a curved spine and bent knees.
I started a weekend job at a bookshop. The owner, Mr. Rao, wants me to arrange the new stock.
That sounds like a pleasant weekend job. Arranging new stock is a good way to learn where everything lives. Take your time and keep similar books together so customers can find them.
Mr. Rao said to put the school textbooks near the door, because students come in first for those.
That is sensible. Putting the textbooks near the door means students find them quickly and do not need to ask. Keep the heavy ones on lower shelves so they are easy to lift.
What if a student asks for a textbook I can't find near the door?
Be honest and polite. Say you will check, then ask Mr. Rao or look at the stock list. Since he wanted the textbooks near the door, tell him about any missing title so he can restock it.
Varun at my office keeps eating lunch alone and I think he's lonely. I've never really spoken to him.
It is kind that you noticed. You do not need a big gesture. Start with a simple, friendly hello, or ask if he would like to join you for lunch.
What if he says no?
Then smile and say maybe another day. Some people need a few invitations before they feel comfortable. Saying no today does not mean he did not appreciate it.
I'll ask Varun to join me tomorrow. What can I talk about, since he always eats alone?

Ask something light, like what he usually eats or how his week is going. Since Varun is used to eating alone, keep it easy and short, so he does not feel pressured, and let him answer at his own pace.
I want to invite my neighbours for chai on Sunday. Is that a good idea?
It is a lovely idea. A small chai evening is an easy way to know your neighbours better. How many families live nearby, and do you have space at home for them?
Three families on our floor. I have a small living room.
Then keep it simple. Invite them for an hour in the late afternoon, serve chai and a few biscuits, and perhaps move a couple of chairs from the bedroom so everyone can sit.
One family is Gauri's, she has a baby. Is that a problem?
Not at all, but think about the baby. Keep the room quiet, put small things out of reach, and give Gauri a comfortable seat where she can keep the baby close.
Good point. Should I send a message or knock on their doors?
Knocking on the door is warmer, and it lets you say hello in person. If someone is out, leave a short note with the day and time of the invitation.
I will knock this evening. What should I remember about Gauri?
Remember that Gauri has a baby, so offer her a comfortable seat and keep the room calm and tidy. Keep hot cups of chai well out of the baby's reach.

That is a great way to practise. Ask Ishita to pretend to be a new classmate, and say your question out loud a few times until it feels easy.

Why are puddles gone much faster on a sunny afternoon than on a cloudy one?
The sun dries them faster. Because sunshine warms the water, and warm water evaporates into the air more quickly than cool water.
Why does a steel nail sink while a huge steel ship floats?

The ship's shape lets it push aside a lot of water. Because a hollow, wide ship pushes aside a weight of water greater than its own, so the water holds it up, while a small solid nail pushes aside too little.
Why might someone feel nervous about speaking in front of the class, even when they know the topic well?
Speaking to a crowd feels risky. Because they worry about forgetting words or being judged, and that worry makes the heart race even when they are well prepared.
Why does a plant on a windowsill bend towards the window?
It is reaching for light. Because plants need light to make food, and the stem grows faster on the shaded side, which tips the top towards the brighter side.
Why do rooms feel warmer when many people are inside?
Each person gives off heat. Because our bodies make warmth all the time, and in a closed room it adds up with nowhere to go.
I have a test tomorrow and a game tonight. How can I decide what to do?
Think about which matters more and whether both are possible. Because you may be able to study first and play later, and weighing the two helps you avoid regrets.
Why does soap clean greasy hands better than water alone?
Soap grabs grease and water together. Because each soap particle has a grease-loving end and a water-loving end, the grease is lifted off the skin and carried away when you rinse.
Why should we leave a little spare time between two tasks in our day?
A gap soaks up delays. Because tasks often take longer than we expect, a gap stops a delay from spoiling everything that comes next.
Why do people check the weather report before planning a picnic?
They check the report so the picnic is not ruined. Because rain or strong heat would make the day unpleasant, knowing in advance lets them pick a better day.
Why does a snake keep flicking its tongue in and out?

The snake flicks its tongue to smell its surroundings. Because the tongue picks up tiny particles from the air and the ground and brings them to special organs in the mouth, the snake can find food and sense danger.
Why is it a good idea to look at a route before cycling to a new place?
Looking at the route first saves trouble. Because it helps us avoid wrong turns and very busy roads, we reach the place with less stress and more safely.
Why should a pot on the stove never be left alone for long?

Things can go wrong quickly on a stove, so someone should stay nearby. Because food can boil over onto the flame or boil dry and burn, and a fire can start when nobody is there to stop it, a pot should not be left alone.
Why do shadows grow long in the late afternoon?

A low sun throws long shadows. Because light from a low sun reaches objects at a slant, it stretches their shadows far across the ground, while from high overhead it falls almost straight down and the shadow stays short.
Why do farmers choose seeds to match the season?
Seeds need the right weather to grow. Because a crop planted in the wrong season may face cold, drought or flood, matching it to the season gives it the best chance.
Why are green mangoes sour and ripe mangoes sweet?
Ripening turns acids and starch into sugars. Because the fruit changes its chemicals as it matures on the tree or in the store, the sourness fades and the sweetness grows.
Why does a room with no furniture sound echoey?
Sound bounces around the bare room. Because hard walls and floors send the sound back instead of soaking it up, the reflections reach our ears a little after the original voice.
Mother cuts 48 guavas equally for 8 children. How many does each child get?
6. Because 8 x 6 = 48, so each one gets 6 with none left over.
Find the sum of 84 and 95.
179. Because 84 + 95 = 179, adding the tens first and then the ones.
What is 28 + 32?
60. Because 28 + 32 = 60, adding the tens first and then the ones.
Priya is 35 years old and her brother is 10 years older. How old is the brother?
45. Because 35 + 10 = 45, so the brother is 45 years old.

Sherlock Holmes closed his eyes and placed his elbows upon the arms of his chair, with his finger-tips together. "The ideal reasoner," he remarked, "would, when he had once been shown a single fact in all its bearings, deduce from it not only all the chain of events which led up to it but also all the results which would follow from it. As Cuvier could correctly describe a whole animal by the contemplation of a single bone, so the observer who has thoroughly understood one link in a series of incidents should be able to accurately state all the other ones, both before and after. We have not yet grasped the results which the reason alone can attain to. Problems may be solved in the study which have baffled all those who have sought a solution by the aid of their senses. To carry the art, however, to its highest pitch, it is necessary that the reasoner should be able to utilise all the facts which have come to his knowledge; and this in itself implies, as you will readily see, a possession of all knowledge, which, even in these days of free education and encyclopaedias, is a somewhat rare accomplishment. It is not so impossible, however, that a man should possess all knowledge which is likely to be useful to him in his work, and this I have endeavoured in my case to do. If I remember rightly, you on one occasion, in the early days of our friendship, defined my limits in a very precise fashion."

Holmes says a perfect thinker could work out a whole chain of events from one fact, just as a scientist can describe an animal from one bone. To do that, a person needs all the useful knowledge for their work, which Holmes has tried to gain.
